errorCodes.meaning: The recipient holds no group state for this room.
`member` has no leaf in the group.
`member` is the recipient's own leaf. A key holder does not remove itself; an owner leaving a room hands it on with rooms/owner/transfer.
The recipient holds no key by `signingKeyId`, or the key is not one its caller may name — or the request names none and the room is not `private`, so the withdrawal cannot be signed. Nothing changed.
The recipient holds no authority credential conferring `admin` on this room for its caller, so it can neither deliver the withdrawal nor advance the room's epoch at the host.

The host is at a different epoch than the recipient's group — another admin advanced the room. The withdrawal, if it was accepted, stays in force. Catch up (rooms/epoch/commits) and try again. The host's epoch is carried in `details.hostEpoch`.

The named host could not be resolved, advertises no transport this recipient speaks, or did not answer. The outcome is unknown, so the recipient keeps the pending removal and the next request to it settles it (item 8). `details.stage` says which step went unanswered; a `private` room's removal has no `revocation` step.

An earlier removal from this room was still pending at the recipient, and when it delivered that removal's revocation list to the host again (item 8) the host refused it. The earlier removal did not take effect: `details.member` is still in the group, and is withdrawn at the host only if `details.listKept` is true and the host ever accepted that list. Nothing of this request was done, and the earlier removal is no longer pending, so repeating this request proceeds; remove `details.member` again if that is still wanted. The host's own code is in `details.code`.

The host answered and declined. `details.stage` says which step: at `revocation` nothing changed; at `advance` the group is unchanged, and on an `attributed` room the withdrawal is in force at the host. The host's own code is in `details.code`.

DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Response.description: Success response to rooms/owner/group/remove. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4#response. Whether the member was withdrawn at the host, the revocation list in force there when they were, and the room's new epoch, which the removed member holds no key for.

epoch.description: The room epoch after the removal, as the host recorded it.

mirrorsPending.description: Mirrors that did not confirm the withdrawal. Each still honours the member's credentials until the list is delivered — with rooms/owner/revoke and no `withdraw`. Absent when every mirror confirmed. Never present when `withdrawn` is false.

revocation.description: The revocation list carrying the withdrawal, as `host` accepted it. Present exactly when `withdrawn` is true.

revokedAt.description: The withdrawal's `revokedAt`: credentials the room issued `member` before it are refused, and fresh ones issued after it are not. Present only when `withdrawn` is true.

withdrawn.description: Whether the member's credentials were withdrawn at the host. True on an attributed room, with `revocation` and `revokedAt`; false on a private room, whose host cannot be told whom to refuse: the member's credentials stay valid there until they expire, and only a reset of every credential (rooms/owner/revoke, a `room` entry) withdraws them. A surface MUST NOT report false as a withdrawal.

Response.title: Rooms Owner Group Remove — response payload

RevocationHead.description: Which `RevocationList` a party holds, without its entries: comparable between the room's key holder and a host, and between two hosts, without disclosing whom the room withdrew.

digest.description: SHA-256 multihash of the list's RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, `proof` included. Two parties holding one sequence with different digests have been given two lists the room signed at one sequence.

RevocationHead.title: RevocationHead

schema.description: A room's owner asks their own agent to remove a member from a sealed room: on an attributed room withdraw every credential the room gave them, at its host at once, and on either sealed tier remove their leaf from the room's MLS group and advance its epoch. 0.4 removes a private room's member from the group, withdrawing nothing, where 0.2 and 0.3 refused.

host.description: The room's host, as a DID: where the withdrawal, if any, is delivered first and the room's epoch advances.

member.description: The DID whose leaf is removed and, on a room that is not private, whose credentials the room withdraws. Never the recipient's own leaf.

mirrors.description: Any other host serving the room, as DIDs. On a room that is not private, each is delivered the withdrawal too: a host that does not hold it honours the member's credentials still. Unused on a private room.

reason.description: Why, carried to the host's epoch advance. Untrusted and attributed to its author: it MUST NOT carry personal data or a credential. Never put into the revocation list.

roomId.description: The room whose group loses a member. The recipient MUST hold its group and a signing key for it.

signingKeyId.description: Which held key signs the room's revocation list as the room, named explicitly as for rooms/owner/revoke. Required unless the room is private, whose removal signs nothing as the room: a request naming none for any other room is refused with noSigningKey.

until.description: OPTIONAL. When the last credential the room issued `member` expires, after which the withdrawal can be dropped from the room's list. Unused on a private room.

schema.title: Rooms Owner Group Remove — payload
